heroHeadline: Moldova Protests Russian Plan for 17 Duma Election Polling Stations in Transnistria
heroSubtitle: Transnistrian leader Vadim Krasnoselsky said Russia intends to open 17 polling stations across the breakaway region for the September 18-20 Russian State Duma election — far beyond the single Chisinau station, at the Russian Embassy, that Moldova's constitutional authorities have authorised. Moldova's Foreign Ministry first objected on August 31, and on September 2 Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi said Chisinau was preparing a formal note of protest, warning that any unauthorised station would be regarded as an unfriendly move. The dispute lands as the EU's September 1 COELA meeting again failed to open accession clusters 2-3 for Moldova, with Hungary repeating its offer to advance only Moldova's cluster 3 alone — an approach the rest of the Council continues to reject — and as the airspace-breach count from the August drone crisis holds at thirteen crossings since August 9.
